project.title: Study-session tracker
project.brief: Build a small local Python program that records study sessions without sending data to a server.
steps: Define a dataclass for topic and non-negative minutes; test valid and invalid data.
Store sessions in a list and use a generator to select sessions longer than 20 minutes.
Save and load JSON using a context manager and explicit UTF-8 encoding; handle missing or malformed files.
Write unit tests for empty data, invalid minutes and a save/load round trip in a temporary directory.

quiz.question: What does a generator do when it reaches yield?
quiz.explanation: A generator preserves its state and resumes when another value is requested.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a with block?
options: Guarantee that every exception is ignored
Manage setup and cleanup of a resource
quiz.explanation: A context manager handles entry and exit, including cleanup when an exception occurs.

quiz.question: What does await do in an asyncio coroutine?
quiz.explanation: Await can yield control while an awaitable is pending; CPU-bound work can still block.

project.title: Task API design
project.brief: Build and test a small task API locally; do not deploy development settings or real secrets.
steps: Define and validate a task request model with a bounded title and appropriate HTTP responses.
Add a SQLAlchemy model and a persistent development database, with a migration reviewed before use.
Add isolated API tests for valid and invalid requests, including database rollback between tests.
Document authentication, trusted key rotation, HTTPS, backups and rollback before considering deployment.

quiz.question: What should a service validate on a signed JWT?
options: Signature and required claims such as expiry and audience
quiz.explanation: A verified signature plus required claims such as issuer and audience are needed.

quiz.question: What does a database transaction commit do?
quiz.explanation: A commit persists the transaction; it does not replace a backup.

quiz.question: What should happen before applying an autogenerated migration?
options: Apply it to production without reading
Review it and test on a disposable database
quiz.explanation: Generated migrations need review and testing, particularly with existing data.

project.title: Safe session reader
project.brief: Write a small C program that reads and summarizes study-session values safely.
steps: Define a struct with fields for topic and minutes, documenting who owns each value.
Read a bounded line and parse minutes using strtol, rejecting malformed or out-of-range input.
Allocate any dynamic collection with overflow and null checks; free each successful allocation.
Compile with warnings and sanitizers when available; test empty input and long lines.

quiz.question: Which action avoids using freed memory?
options: Stop using the pointer after free
quiz.explanation: An allocation must not be accessed or freed again after it is released.

quiz.question: Why check count against SIZE_MAX / element_size?
options: To guard against size multiplication overflow
quiz.explanation: The check prevents wrapping the requested allocation size.

quiz.question: Why check the result of tmpfile?
options: It always returns a valid stream
quiz.explanation: A null stream indicates failure and must not be used.

project.title: Typed task collection
project.brief: Create a small Rust command-line task collection using safe ownership and explicit errors.
steps: Define a Task struct and an impl method that borrows the task for display.
Store tasks in a Vec and iterate by reference without consuming the collection.
Parse user input into Result and report invalid input without unwrap on untrusted values.
Add tests for empty data, valid input and an error case; explain any lifetime annotation you introduce.

quiz.question: What does &self mean in a method?
options: A shared borrow of the receiver
quiz.explanation: A shared borrow lets the method read without taking ownership.

quiz.question: What does ? do for an Err result?
options: Returns the error early to the caller
quiz.explanation: The operator propagates the error through a compatible return type.

quiz.question: What does a lifetime annotation do?
quiz.explanation: Lifetimes describe borrow relationships; they do not extend the actual lifetime.

project.title: Accessible study list
project.brief: Build a small task list in a local web project using the browser or React.
steps: Render tasks with labels and buttons; use textContent or escaped React output for user text.
Add a way to create and complete tasks using event delegation or component state.
Use a mock or real same-origin endpoint with loading, HTTP-error and retry states; never claim the API exists unless you implement it.
Test with keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels; document setup and known limitations.

quiz.question: When fetch receives HTTP 404, what normally happens?
quiz.explanation: HTTP errors still produce a response; check its status.

quiz.question: What should React effect cleanup do for an interval?
quiz.explanation: Cleanup prevents the timer from continuing after the effect is disposed.

quiz.question: Why use textContent for untrusted text?
options: It inserts text without parsing markup
quiz.explanation: textContent prevents the input from being interpreted as markup.

project.title: Repeatable development workflow
project.brief: Set up a safe local repository, automated test and container build for a small application.
steps: Create a disposable repository with a README and a minimal application; do not add secrets.
Add a real test and run it locally, then configure CI to run the same test on pull requests.
Create a minimal container image, run as a non-root user and document required writable paths.
Practice a cherry-pick on local branches; document image versioning, rollback and backup steps.

quiz.question: What does git rebase generally do?
options: Replays commits onto a different base
quiz.explanation: Rebase commonly creates new commit IDs; coordinate before rewriting shared history.

quiz.question: What does a green CI check demonstrate?
options: Configured checks passed for that run
quiz.explanation: Tests have scope and cannot prove absence of all problems.

quiz.question: What is a Docker image?
options: A build artifact used to create containers
quiz.explanation: Images and running containers are distinct.

project.title: Responsible classification experiment
project.brief: Train and evaluate a small classifier and record its limitations; use non-sensitive data.
steps: Load a documented dataset and separate training and test data before fitting.
Use a preprocessing pipeline and train a baseline classifier; set a random seed for reproducibility.
Report held-out metrics and a confusion matrix, discussing the sample size and potential errors.
Write a model card describing data, limitations and intended use; do not claim production readiness.

quiz.question: Where should a scaler learn its parameters?
quiz.explanation: Fitting preprocessing on test data leaks information into training.

quiz.question: Does a detailed prompt guarantee accuracy?
options: No; verify claims and generated code
quiz.explanation: Outputs can still be incorrect regardless of where the model runs.

quiz.question: Why keep the test set separate from model selection?
options: To estimate performance on data not used for tuning
quiz.explanation: Reusing the test set for tuning can make the final estimate optimistic.
